title: Coverage Quality Analysis — Genuine Gap vs Scope Mismatch
question: Does 36.63% represent (A) genuine testing weakness, (B) scope mismatch, (C) configuration/architecture issue, or (D) a combination?

verdict.secondary_label: GENUINE TESTING WEAKNESS — residual, confined, and OUTSIDE the current engine-testing campaign

attribution.scope_mismatch_share: dominant — accounts for the entire 28.96-point difference between 36.63% and 65.59%
attribution.genuine_weakness_share: residual — confined to transaction_intelligence (24.25%), financial_intelligence (34.82%), repositories (55.42%), balance (58.95%)

verdict.configuration_issue_C: NOT PRESENT as a coverage-measurement defect. .coveragerc is coherent and its omit list is documented and justified. One reporting defect WAS found, but in the MUTATION runner (post-run config restoration), not in coverage.

evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.claim: The 36.63% figure is a test-scope artifact, fully reproducible on demand.
evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.evidence: Running `pytest --cov=src --cov-config=.coveragerc tests/unit/engines/` reproduces 843 passed / 3916 covered / 6322 missing / 36.63% — matching every M9-C42.18 number exactly. Running the same coverage config over `tests/` yields 1745 passed / 7111 covered / 3127 missing / 65.59%.

evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.claim: Identical statement population proves it is not a configuration difference.
evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.evidence: Both runs measure exactly 10,238 statements under the identical .coveragerc. Only the executing test population differs (843 vs 1746 tests).

evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.claim: Five whole source areas measure 0.00% under the subset purely because no engine unit test can reach them.
evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.evidence: services 0.00% -> 66.29% (2047 stmts); common 0.00% -> 99.38%; cashflow 0.00% -> 97.56%; orchestration 0.00% -> 80.28%; other 0.00% -> 78.49%. These are exercised by capability, property, contract, golden, and domain suites that tests/unit/engines/ excludes.

evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.claim: The threshold's own companion policy proves 40% was never an engine-only threshold.
evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.evidence: .github/scripts/check_coverage_threshold.py sets engines=70 SEPARATELY from overall=40. Applying the backend-wide 40% aggregate to an engine-only test subset mismatches the threshold to a population it was not designed for.

evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.claim: The threshold was originally calibrated against a broad unit population, not an engine subset.
evidence_for_B_scope_mismatch.evidence: Origin commit f0e28f0b calibrated 40% while adding 189 tests across money.py, calculations.py, formatting.py, parsing.py, errors.py — none of which live under tests/unit/engines/.

evidence_for_A_residual_genuine_weakness.assessment: GENUINE LOW COVERAGE under the full suite. Not explained by scope.
GENUINE LOW COVERAGE under the full suite. Largest single missing-statement contributor (526).
MODERATE. Below its own intended 40% threshold? No — 55.42% EXCEEDS the repositories=40 intended threshold. Not a gate failure.
MODERATE and small in absolute terms (39 statements). balance_engine is in ENGINE_SELECTION but was NOT part of the four-engine M9-C42.17/18/19 mutation campaign.
ACCEPTABLE against the services=40 intended threshold (66.29% >> 40%). Largest area by statement count, so its 690 missing statements dominate absolute counts without indicating a gate failure.

evidence_against_C_configuration_issue.evidence: source = src with a documented, justified omit list: tests/conftest (never measure tests), entry points (main/startup/api/health — bootstrap only), extraction pipeline (requires PDF/binary I/O, explicitly deferred to integration/contract tests), routers (HTTP layer), tools/scripts, and cache/venv directories. Each exclusion carries an inline rationale comment.
evidence_against_C_configuration_issue.verdict: COHERENT — no unintended source population detected

evidence_against_C_configuration_issue.claim: branch=True is active and correctly reflected in the reported percentage.
evidence_against_C_configuration_issue.evidence: Verified arithmetic: (7111 covered_lines + 1401 covered_branches) / (10238 statements + 2740 branches) = 65.59%, matching coverage.py's reported percent_covered exactly.

evidence_against_C_configuration_issue.claim: 195 source files measured, spanning every non-omitted area.
evidence_against_C_configuration_issue.evidence: Full-suite coverage.json contains 195 file entries totalling 10,238 statements across engines, services, repositories, core, models, common, orchestration.

p0_engine_coverage_under_full_suite.conclusion: Every engine in the mutation campaign massively exceeds the 70% intended engine threshold. There is no coverage-driven justification for adding tests to these engines.

decision_on_adding_coverage_tests.rationale: The canonical full-suite command already reports 65.59% and pytest-cov emits 'Required test coverage of 40.0% reached'. The gate PASSES. Adding tests to raise a percentage that already passes would be pure metric manipulation and is explicitly forbidden.
decision_on_adding_coverage_tests.genuine_gaps_note: These are documented as real, evidence-backed opportunities. They are OUTSIDE the current four-engine mutation campaign and were NOT addressed in this phase, because this phase's mandate was to establish metrics rather than optimize them.

final_statement: 36.63% did NOT represent a genuine testing weakness in the engines under campaign. It was a scope-mismatch artifact of measuring a backend-wide aggregate threshold against an engine-only test subset. The authoritative full-suite measurement is 65.59%, which PASSES the unchanged 40% gate. A residual, genuine, and clearly bounded coverage weakness exists in transaction_intelligence and financial_intelligence, both outside the current campaign.
